output.summary: Build a URL shortener service in Java 25 / Spring Boot 4. A write endpoint (POST /api/v1/urls) creates short codes from a base62-encoded globally unique counter in Redis (batched INCRBY 1000) with a DB-sequence fallback recorded in code_source; a read endpoint (GET /{short_code}) issues 302 redirects with Cache-Control: private, using a Redis cache in front of Postgres, which is the source of truth (Flyway migrations). Read and write paths are independently deployable via Spring profiles. Deliverables include a global exception handler emitting problem+json, a committed OpenAPI document, unit and Testcontainers integration tests, a Dockerfile, and a README. Authentication and analytics are out of scope.

stories.i_want: to POST a long URL (optionally with a custom alias and expiration date) to /api/v1/urls and receive a short URL
stories.so_that: I can share a compact link instead of the full URL

stories.as_a: end user following a short link
stories.i_want: GET /{short_code} to redirect me to the original long URL
stories.so_that: I reach the intended destination transparently

stories.i_want: short codes generated from a globally unique Redis counter (batched INCRBY 1000) with a DB sequence fallback recorded as code_source
stories.so_that: codes are guaranteed unique and generation survives Redis outages

stories.i_want: the read path to check a Redis cache (short_code -> long_url, TTL <= expiry) before hitting Postgres, and to bypass the cache with logged degradation when Redis is down
stories.so_that: redirects are fast and the service remains available during cache outages

stories.i_want: read and write paths deployable as separate instances via Spring profiles (read, write, and a combined default)
stories.so_that: I can scale redirect traffic independently of link-creation traffic

stories.i_want: a global exception handler producing problem+json, a committed OpenAPI document, unit and Testcontainers integration tests, a Dockerfile, and a README
stories.so_that: the service is well-documented, testable, and deployable

acceptance_criteria.given: a running write instance and a valid request body with long_url = https://example.com/some/path
acceptance_criteria.then: the service responds 201 with a JSON body containing short_url built from the configured base URL (default http://localhost:8080) plus a generated base62 short code, and a row exists in the Postgres urls table with short_code, long_url, created_at, code_source, and created_by left null

acceptance_criteria.given: a request with long_url that is not a valid http/https URL, exceeds 2048 characters, or uses another scheme (e.g., ftp://)
acceptance_criteria.then: the service responds 400 with Content-Type application/problem+json describing the validation failure and no row is persisted

acceptance_criteria.given: a request with custom_alias = 'promo2024' where that alias/short_code already exists in the urls table
acceptance_criteria.then: the service responds 409 with application/problem+json and the existing mapping is unchanged

acceptance_criteria.given: a long_url that has already been shortened previously
acceptance_criteria.when: the client sends POST /api/v1/urls with the same long_url and no custom_alias
acceptance_criteria.then: the service responds 201 with a new, distinct short code (no 409, no deduplication)

acceptance_criteria.given: a request with custom_alias containing characters outside [0-9a-zA-Z] or with length < 3 or > 32
a request with an expiration_date that is malformed ISO-8601 or is in the past

acceptance_criteria.then: the service responds 302 with Location set to the stored long_url and header Cache-Control: private

acceptance_criteria.given: a short_code that does not exist in cache or database
a short code whose expires_at is in the past
Redis is available and the write instance's local counter batch is exhausted
acceptance_criteria.when: a new short code is requested
acceptance_criteria.then: the service issues INCRBY 1000 on the global Redis counter, allocates codes as base62 encodings of counter values, and persists code_source = 'redis'; codes are unique across concurrent instances

acceptance_criteria.given: Redis is unavailable during short-code generation
acceptance_criteria.then: the service falls back to a Postgres sequence for the counter value, responds 201, and persists code_source = 'db_sequence' (or equivalent documented value)

acceptance_criteria.given: a short code whose mapping is present in the Redis cache
acceptance_criteria.then: the service serves the redirect from the cache without querying Postgres, and cache entries carry a TTL no greater than the remaining time to expires_at

acceptance_criteria.given: Redis is unavailable on the read path
acceptance_criteria.when: the client sends GET /{short_code} for an existing code
acceptance_criteria.then: the service bypasses the cache, serves the 302 redirect directly from Postgres, and logs the cache degradation

acceptance_criteria.given: an instance started with the 'read' Spring profile
acceptance_criteria.then: the service responds 404 because write controllers are not registered; conversely, an instance started with the 'write' profile responds 404 to GET /{short_code}, and the default combined profile serves both

acceptance_criteria.when: the build and test suite run
acceptance_criteria.then: Flyway migrations create the urls table (short_code PK, long_url, created_at, expires_at, created_by, code_source), a committed OpenAPI document matches the implemented endpoints, unit tests and Testcontainers-based integration tests (Postgres and Redis) pass, and a Dockerfile and README are present

acceptance_criteria.given: any error response produced by the API (400, 404, 409, 410, and unhandled 500s)
acceptance_criteria.then: it is produced by the global exception handler with Content-Type application/problem+json and a consistent problem-details body

non_goals: Authentication or authorization of any endpoint
Analytics, click tracking, or usage statistics (deferred to a later scenario)
Populating the created_by column (nullable, left null in this scenario)
Python/FastAPI implementation (target stack for this run is Java)
Custom short-domain management, link editing, or link deletion endpoints

ambiguities.question: What TTL should the Redis cache entry use when a URL has no expiration_date?
options: A fixed configurable default TTL (e.g., 24 hours)
A short TTL (e.g., 5 minutes) to bound staleness
ambiguities.default_if_unanswered: A fixed configurable default TTL of 24 hours

ambiguities.question: Are gaps in the code sequence acceptable when an instance restarts and discards the unused remainder of its 1000-value Redis batch?
options: Yes, gaps are acceptable (simplest, standard approach)
No, unused ranges must be persisted and reclaimed on restart

ambiguities.question: Should generated (non-custom) short codes also be validated/guaranteed to fall within the 3-32 length constraint, e.g., by offsetting the counter so codes start at length 3?
options: Yes, seed/offset the counter so generated codes are at least 3 characters
No, generated codes may be shorter than 3 characters; the length rule applies only to custom aliases
ambiguities.default_if_unanswered: Yes, seed the counter so generated codes are at least 3 characters, keeping one uniform code format

assumptions: Custom aliases and short codes must match [0-9a-zA-Z] with length 3-32; violations return 400 with application/problem+json (per AMB-1 answer)
409 applies only to a taken custom_alias; re-posting an already-shortened long_url creates a new distinct short code (per AMB-2 answer)
Only http and https schemes are accepted for long_url, with a maximum length of 2048 characters; violations return 400 problem+json (per AMB-3 answer)
created_by is a nullable column left null in this scenario (per AMB-4 answer)
Both malformed ISO-8601 and past expiration_date values are rejected with 400 problem+json (per AMB-5 answer)
When Redis is unavailable on the read path, the service bypasses the cache and serves redirects directly from Postgres, logging the degradation (per AMB-6 answer)
Spring profiles 'read', 'write', and a default combined profile conditionally register controllers; a read instance returns 404 for write endpoints and vice versa (per AMB-7 answer)
The short_url base is a configurable application property defaulting to http://localhost:8080 (per AMB-8 answer)
Target stack is Java 25 / Spring Boot 4 (SDLC_TARGET_STACK=java for this run); Flyway is used for migrations
